chunks: When you complete your sa‘i, descend from al-Marwah and trim some hair from the sides of your head, from your eyebrows, and from your beard. Take from your mustache and clip your nails, leaving some of them for your hajj. When you do that, you have exited from everything from which you had entered ihram, and it is permissible for you to perform tawaf of the House voluntarily as much as you wish. There is no harm in praying the two rak‘ahs of voluntary tawaf wherever you wish in the mosque, but it is only permissible to pray the two rak‘ahs of the obligatory tawaf at the Maqam.

When it is the Day of Tarwiyah, perform ghusl, wear your two garments, and enter al-Masjid al-Haram barefoot, with tranquility and dignity upon you. Perform seven circuits around the House voluntarily, and if you wish then pray two rak‘ahs for your tawaf at the Maqam of Ibrahim عليه السلام or in the Hijr, and sit until the sun declines. When the sun declines, pray six rak‘ahs before the obligatory prayer, then perform the obligatory prayer and begin ihram after Zuhr, or if you wish after ‘Asr, for hajj ifrad, saying:

"There is no god but Allah, the Forbearing, the Generous. There is no god but Allah, the Most High, the Magnificent. Glory be to Allah, Lord of the seven heavens and Lord of the seven earths, and whatever is in them, and whatever is between them, and whatever is beneath them, and Lord of the Mighty Throne. And praise belongs to Allah, Lord of the worlds.

O Allah, I ask You to make me among those who answer You, believe in Your promise, and follow Your Book and Your command. For I am Your servant and within Your grasp. I do not protect myself except from what You protect, and I do not take except what You have given.

O Allah, I intend that which You have commanded of hajj according to Your Book and the sunnah of Your Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله. So strengthen me for what I am weak in, make it easy for me, accept it from me, and receive my rites from me in ease from You and well-being. Make me among Your delegation and the pilgrims of Your House, those with whom You are pleased, whom You have approved, named, and written.
O Allah, grant me the completion of my rites in ease from You and well-being, help me in it, and accept it from me.

O Allah, if some obstacle should arise that restrains me, then release me where You restrain me, by Your decree which You have decreed against me, and turn away from me the evil of the decree and the evil of destiny.

I enter into ihram for You with my face, my hair, my skin, my flesh, my blood, my marrow, my bones, and my sinews, from women, perfume, and garments, seeking by that Your noble countenance and the final abode."

Then recite quietly the four obligatory talbiyahs, if you wish standing, if you wish sitting, and if you wish at the door of the mosque while you are going out from it, facing the Black Stone, saying:
"Here I am, O Allah, here I am. Here I am, You have no partner, here I am. Indeed all praise, blessing, and sovereignty belong to You. You have no partner."

Then proceed, with tranquility and dignity upon you, with tasbih, tahlil, and the remembrance of Allah عز وجل. When you reach al-Raqta' before al-Radm, which is the meeting-point of the two roads, until you overlook al-Abtah, then raise your voice in the talbiyah until you come to Mina. And recite the talbiyah as you recited in the ‘umrah, and say frequently: "Dhi al-Ma‘arij," for the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله used to say it often.
And say, while heading to Mina: "O Allah, in You alone do I place my hope, and to You alone do I supplicate, so let me attain my hope, and set right for me my deed."

When you come to Mina, say: "Praise belongs to Allah, who brought me to it sound and in well-being, and caused me to reach this place. O Allah, this is Mina, and it is among those rites by which You have favored Your awliya'. So I ask You to send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, and to bestow upon me therein what You bestowed upon Your awliya' and the people of obedience to You, for I am only Your servant and within Your grasp."

Then pray there al-Maghrib, al-‘Isha al-Akhirah, and al-Fajr in Masjid al-Khayf. Let your prayer in it be near the minaret that is in the middle of the mosque, within thirty cubits from all its sides. That is the mosque of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم and the prayer-place of the Prophets who prayed there before him عليهم السلام. Whatever lies outside thirty cubits around it from every side is not part of the mosque.

key_terms.التَّقْصِيرِ: trimming the hair to exit the state of ihram for ‘umrah
key_terms.التَّلْبِيَةِ: the formula recited upon entering ihram and during the journey of hajj
key_terms.الْإِحْرَامَ: the consecrated state entered for hajj with intention and talbiyah
key_terms.الْمَقَامِ: Maqam Ibrahim, the required place for the prayer of obligatory tawaf
key_terms.سَعْيِكَ: the ritual walking between al-Safa and al-Marwah
key_terms.مَسْجِدِ الْخَيْفِ: the mosque in Mina where the pilgrim is instructed to pray
key_terms.مِنًى: the sacred site to which the pilgrim proceeds on the Day of Tarwiyah
key_terms.يَوْمُ التَّرْوِيَةِ: the eighth day of Dhu al-Hijjah when the pilgrim prepares for hajj

ai.seo_question: What should a pilgrim do after sa‘i and on the Day of Tarwiyah before going to Mina?
ai.summary: This passage outlines the rulings and supplications connected to taqsir after sa‘i, the renewal of ihram for hajj on the Day of Tarwiyah, and the journey to Mina. It combines fiqh instructions with prescribed adhkar and du'as, while also identifying the prayer location in Masjid al-Khayf and invoking the sunnah of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم.
